Commentary.Commentary: The third innings is set to begin. Pakistan players take the field. Followed by Tom Latham and Devon Conway who walk out to open for New Zealand.
... Third innings ...

Right then, the Kiwis wrap things up in just a single over, as Ish Sodhi takes the final wicket to hand his side a lead of 41 runs when they come out to bat. Pakistan could cross the 400-run mark thanks to Saud Shakeel's long stay at the crease. He managed to hold one end intact by facin 341 deliveries. He played a crucial knock to et his side back into the game. Sarfaraz Ahmed also imprssed with his half-ton but could not convert it into three digits. For Kiwis, it is their spinners that worked well in tandem and caused all kinds of problems in the final session of moving day. They picked up 4 wickts in that session to put Pakistan 9 down. On the morning session, they did not waste much time to take the final wicket. New Zealand now have to bat throughout the day and score at a brisk rate, if they wish to win this Test match. Do join us shortly for New Zealand's response.

OUT! LBW! So, Ish Sodhi gets the final wicket here. Abrar Ahmed takes the review instantly. It is tossed up, around off, turns in a touch. Abrar Ahmed tries to defend it out but misses. He gets rapped on his pads. It looks plumb and the umpire raises his finger. The review also does not save the batter here as the Ball Tracking confirms three reds.
Flatter one, on off. Saud Shakeel rocks back and hit it down to long on. They take one.
Saud Shakeel goes back and works it to the leg side.
On middle and leg, nudged to mid-wicket.
Sarfaraz Ahmed tries to sweep but misses.
Floats it up, wide of off. It grips and turns in. Shakeel defends it back to the bowler.

The morning session on Day 4 is set to begin. Both the umpires make their way out on the field. The Kiwis players are seen to be in a huddle before taking the field. Soon, Saud Shakeel and Abrar Ahmed walk out with their blades. It will be Ish Sodhi to start with the ball.

The New Zealand bowlers toiled hard through the day with Tim Southee taking the wicket of Imam-ul-Haq in the first session and Daryl Mitchell claiming the scalp of Sarfaraz Ahmed just before Tea. Late in the day, as the ball started to get older, the spinners began to come into play which allowed Ajaz Patel and Ish Sodhi to claim two wickets each. Tom Latham dropped a golden opportunity to dismiss the centurion off Tim Southee’s bowling and put down another tough chance at silly point later. The Kiwis will want to make sure they take their opportunities in the field especially when it is offered so sparingly. After a sluggish start, the moving day of Test cricket gathered momentum right at the end and we now anticipate a thrilling morning session on Day 4. Stay tuned.

Hello, and welcome back, ladies and gentlemen to our coverage of Day 4 of the second Test between Pakistan and New Zealand at the National Stadium in Karachi. The hosts looked like they were in the driver's seat for most of Day 3 but they seemed to be maneuvering this game toward a draw. They managed to preserve their wickets losing just two up until the last hour of the day. They maintained a low scoring rate and despite playing throughout the entire day they are still 42 runs behind the New Zealand score. They suffered a collapse just before stumps losing 4 wickets for 12 runs but the centurion Saud Shakeel is still unbeaten and Pakistan will be hoping he can frustrate the visitors.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

New Zealand were made to toil hard in the sun throughout the moving day but they head back with smiles across their faces. As the second new ball became older, it started to find some assistance off the deck. Ajaz Patel and Ish Sodhi bowled in tandem which finally paid dividends once Ajaz Patel got rid of Agha Salman. This wicket was the turning point of this day, because the hosts were unable to keep things under control. The two spinners combined for four wickets - two each. This will surely revive the hopes of the vistors and would be eager to take the final wicket early on Day 4. Kiwis might feel they have their noses in front here, although there is still a long way to go for us to get a concrete result. Do join us on 5th January 2023 at 10.30 am IST (5 am GMT) to find out how things pan out in the morning session on Day 4. Until then, take care and goodbye.

Not a great end to the day for Pakistan. This game has slightly tilted in favour of New Zealand as the hosts still trail by 42 runs. Saud Shakeel and Agha Salman came out to bat in the post-Tea session and started really well by putting away the bad balls. Although, once this stand was broken, Saud Shakeel could hardly find an able partner and witnessed his team falling apart from one end. Now, it is all down to him as Pakistan will hope he can continue well alongside Abrar Ahmed in the morning session on Day 4 and frustrate New Zealand by giving them a taste of their own medicine just as Matt Henry and Ajaz Patel troubled them in the first innings for the final wicket.

An riveting session of Test cricket. It is the visitors who head back into the dressing room as the happier side. Pakistan will be a tad disappointed with the way their lower-middle order succumbed to the spin attack. This session saw a total of 31 over being bowled wherein Pakistan scored 70 runs but also lost 4 wickets to put them in a precarious position.
This is full, coming in with the arm, Abrar Ahmed prods and blocks it to the leg side. So, Abrar Ahmed does defend the final delivery solidly and THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 3.
A single now as this is swept to square leg. Abrar Ahmed needs to survive one delivery before stumps.
Fuller, just outside off. Shakeel goes back and smothers it out.
Flatter, outside off. Shakeel plays it late to point.
Outside off, blocked out on the front foot.
Fuller, outside off. Shakeel dabs it to slip.
Gives it a lot of air this time. Full and wide outside off. Ahmed dabs it out.
This one turns in from outside off. Ahmed goes back and nudges it to short leg.
Pushed through quicker, wide of off. Ahmed looks to chase it but misses.
NO BALL! A high full toss, it slips off his hands. No ball for height.
Bowls a flipper this time but fires this down leg side. Abrar Ahmed leaves this one alone.
This is full as well and wide outside off. Abrar Ahmed cuts this to the right of slip who stops it well.
Loopy delivery bowled full and outside the off. Abrar Ahmed knocks this towards cover.
FOUR! Two boundaries in a row! Ajaz Patel bowls this short and outside off. Saud Shakeel pulls this towards deep mid-wicket for four more runs.
FOUR! Stand and deliver! Ajaz Patel floats this one full and outside off. Saud Shakeel lofts this towards long off for four runs.
Full once again and outside the off stump. Saud Shakeel happy to block this away.
Continues bowling full and outside off. Saud Shakeel defends this towards cover.
Bowls this full and in line with stumps. Saud Shakeel defends this back down the pitch.
Fires this one wide outside the off stump. Saud Shakeel leaves this alone.
This is slightly short and in line with the stumps. Abrar Ahmed manages to keep this one out.

OUT! BOWLED! Ish Sodhi is on a HAT-TRICK and New Zealand have dug deep to wrench the advantage back in their favor. Ish Sodhi flights this one full and outside the off pole. Mir Hamza takes a long stride forward and looks to defend this but leaves a gap between bat and pad. The ball turns sharply after pitching and creeps into the gap to peg back the stumps. The New Zealand players are ecstatic as they have had very little to cheer all day but they will be delighted by the fact that they still have the advantage in this game. Just one wicket more to put an end to Pakistan's inning and it will be Abrar Ahmed who makes his way out to the crease.
Mir Hamza strides out to the middle.

OUT! TIMBER! Ish Sodhi gets his first wicket and Pakistan are crumbling here! Ish Sodhi serves a googly on a shorter length and gets it to come back into the stumps from outside off. Naseem Shah make room to play this through the off side but misses the ball and watches his stumps get shattered. Pakistan lose their eighth wicket and after controlling the entire day find themselves once again on the back foot. New Zealand will now be looking to wrap up the tail before stumps.
Loopy delivery bowled full and outside off. Naseem Shah blocks this to the off side.
FOUR! This has been hoicked away! Ish Sodhi bowls another googly short and into the stumps. Naseem Shah lofts this towards wide long on for four runs.

Ish Sodhi bowls a googly full and outside the off stump. Naseem Shah looks to punch this away but it stays low and Naseem Shah gets a slight inside edge. The ball goes into the keeper's hands and the umpire goes upstairs to check for a catch. The soft signal is not out and replays confirm it bounces before the keeper's gloves.
Goes full and in line with the stumps. Saud Shakeel flicks this towards mid-wicket.
On a good length this time and still outside the off stump. Saud Shakeel shoulders his arms to this one.
Goes slightly fuller this time but still wide outside off. Saud Shakeel raises his bat and lets it through to the keeper.
Bowls this on a good length and just outside off. Rises sharply after bouncing and Saud Shakeel keeps his arms down to let the ball through.

Bowls this on a good length and angles this into the stumps. Saud Shakeel looks to clip this towards the leg side but misses. Gets hit on the pads and there is an appeal but this is going down leg side.
Daryl Mitchell starts with the outside off stump line on a good length. Left alone.

DROPPED! Ajaz Patel bowls this slightly short and outside off, at a quicker pace. Naseem Shah gets forward and pushes at the ball but it hits him high on the bat. The ball goes in the air to the right of silly point where Tom Latham is placed. He sticks his right hand out and gets to the ball but is unable to hold on. It was a difficult chance but another opportunity goes begging.
Pushed through quicker and on off. Shah blocks it to silly point.
Full, and on off. Shah dabs it down.
Angled in full, into the pads. Shah blocks it back to the bowler.
Naseem Shah makes his way out to the middle.

OUT! CAUGHT! Ajaz Patel gets another wicket here. Hasan Ali holes out this time. It is a short ball, around off. Ali rocks back and pulls it towards deep mid-wicket. The ball goes very high in the air, but it is hit straight down the throat of Devon Conway in the deep. He juggles it once before pouching it safely near the ropes. Pakistan are falling apart here.
Commentary.Howout: c Devon Conway b Ajaz Patel

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Almost a catch!. It is a short ball, outside off. Ali goes back and smashes it high to the left of the man at mid off. Matt Henry there moves to his left, puts in a full-stretched dive and manages to get two hands on it mid-air, although it is hit powerfully and races away to the boundary.
FOUR! UP AND OVER! It is overpitced, just outside off. Saud Shakeel gets under it and lofts it over extra cover for a fine boundary.
Mitchell goes full again, wide outside off. Shakeel drives it towards point.
It is full, on off stump. Shakeel gets it to the off side off the outer half.
Good length, outside off. Shakeel shoulders his arms at it.
Length ball, on off. Shakeel defends it out watchfully.
Very full, wide of off, left alone.
Bowls this full and in line with the stumps. Hasan Ali digs this out back towards the bowler.
Around off, Ali blocks it out solidly.
Full, outside off, defended out.
Hasan Ali is the new batter at the crease.

OUT! CAUGHT AT SLIPS! Ajaz Patel gets his second wicket and has broken the stand which was cutting down the deficit for run. Brilliant catch by Michael Bracewell at first slip, he gathers it on his second attempt. It is looped up, full and outside off. Agha Salman gets down on one knee and goes for the sweep. All he manages to get is a top edge. The ball lobs to the right of Michael Bracewell at first slip. The fielder dives to his right and gets a hand on it but it spills out, although Michael Bracewell keeps his eyes on the ball and makes the most of the second bite.
Commentary.Howout: c Michael Bracewell b Ajaz Patel

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Top shot! It is tossed up, full and outside off. Salman dances down the track and lofts it over mid off for a boundary. The stand also moves to 50 now.
Patel comes 'round the wicket and serves it full, coming in with the arm on off. Salman defends it back to the bowler.
Continues bowling full and on an off stump line. Saud Shakeel taps this towards short cover.
A tad bit fuller and still well outside the line of the stumps on the off side. Saud Shakeel raises his arms and lets it through.
Fuller this time and slightly outside the off stump. Saud Shakeel defends this solidly towards short cover.
Goes really full and just outside the off pole. Saud Shakeel digs this out towards mid off.
Bowls this on a good length and outside the off stump. Saud Shakeel continues to be watchful as he lets this through.
Daryl Mitchell bowls this full and wide outside off. Saud Shakeel continues to leave balls that are along that line.
FOUR! Two boundaries in the over! Ish Sodhi floats this full and on a leg stump line. Agha Salman makes room and strokes this towards long on for four runs.
Bowls a googly in line with the stump. Agha Salman gets forward and blocks this into the off side.

Goes 'round the wicket to the right-hander and serves this full, outside leg. Agha Salman pads this away.
A loopy delivery bowled full and outside the off stump. Agha Salman blocks this towards cover.
FOUR! A surprise boundary for Pakistan! Ish Sodhi floats this one full and wide outside off. Agha Salman goes for the expansive drive and drills this to deep point for four runs.
On a length, leaving the left-hander once again. Saud Shakeel deals with it with ease and sees off the over with another sighter.
A length ball, that lands around off and leaves the batter. Saud Shakeel is happy to have a sighter.
On a good length, wide outside off. Saud Shakeel leaves it alone. This is his 305th delivery. It has been a gitty knock by the Pakistani batter.
Full length, around off. Much closer to Shakeel. He blocks it on his front foot this time.
Outside off once again. Saud Shakeel lets it through.
A length ball, angled across the left-hander, outside off. It moves further away which makes it easy for Shakeel to make the leave.

Fuller, outside off. Saud Shakeel gets across and blocks.

Saud Shakeel continues to eat up deliveries but Agha Salman has not been able to play the role of an aggressor yet. This Test looks like it could be headed for a draw but with two days left after this session anything could happen.

Ish Sodhi (17-1-65-0) is back into the attack.

On a good length this time and outside the off stump. Agha Salman defends this towards point.

Gets this one to angle away from the left-hander on a good length and outside off. Saud Shakeel raises his arms and lets the keeper collect the ball.

Attacks the stumps on a fuller length at 133 clicks. Agha Salman knocks this back towards the bowler.

Continues bowling on a good length and outside off. Agha Salman shoulders his arms and leaves it alone.
This is on a good length and just outside off. Nips back in after pitching and Agha Salman manages to keep it out towards point.
Goes full once again and on the pads. Saud Shakeel flicks this wide of mid on and takes a single.
Matt Henry bowls this full and outside the off pole. Saud Shakeel lets this go through to the keeper.

Fires in a yorker this time aimed for the leg stump Agha Salman gets his bat down in time and manages to keep this out.

Strays down leg side on a fuller length. Agha Salman misses his flick and Tom Blundell does well to get across to stop the ball.
Goes fuller this time and angles this away from the left-hander from outside off. Saud Shakeel shoulders arms to this one.

On a good length once again and outside off. Saud Shakeel raises his arms and leaves the ball alone.

The final session on the moving day is set to begin. Saud Shakeel and Agha Salman stride out to the middle with the bat in hand. The Kiwis take the field and we are moments away now. It will be Matt Henry to start with the ball.

The New Zealand bowlers had very little joy in the second session as they were unable to get any purchase from the wicket and the old ball was not providing any reverse swing. Tim Southee opted to bowl his spinners till the new ball became available but it made no difference as the pitch seemed really flat. The introduction of Daryl Mitchell, the man with the golden arm, seemed to have provided them with a spark as he had an LBW decision reversed for a faint edge on his very first delivery before getting a wicket on the thrid ball. The wicket has to be credited to Tom Blundell for his quick glovework behind the stumps. Will they be able to bowl out Pakistan with their lead intact? Join us at 15.30 pm IST (9.50 am GMT) to find out.

Pakistan came out after Lunch with positive intent and scored freely allowing Saud Shakeel to reach his half-century before the new ball was taken. Sarfaraz Ahmed got to his fifty in just 61 deliveries and the partnership between the two began to swell. Saud Shakeel played extremely well to reach his century and when Sarfaraz Ahmed was finally dismissed for 78, the two had added 150 runs in 238 balls. Agha Salman has joined Saud Shakeel in the middle and they will be looking to build another partnership here.

This has been Pakistan’s session through and through barring a solitary wicket that they lost right before the Tea as they have put on 113 runs in 27 overs at a run rate of 4.19. Saud Shakeel and Sarfaraz Ahmed  have helped their side cut down the deficiet considerably and they now trail by just 112 runs with five wickets in hand. New Zealand would be heading into the dressing room much happier than they would have been had the wicket not fallen and will feel that they have a chance to run through the lower order in the last session of the day.

OUT! STUMPED! Some exceptional glovework from Tom Blundell has provided his side with a much-needed breakthrough. Fuller, sliding down leg. Ahmed misses his flick. The keeper gathers it cleanly and whips the bails off. The square leg umpire takes it upstais to confirm. The UltraEdge confirms no bat is involved. The side-on angle suggests that Sarfaraz Ahmed gets his back foot inside the crease, but it looks like Ahmed lifts his leg a touch once the keeper takes the bails off. This is going to be close. New Zealand players are already celebrating here as there seems to be some gap between the foot and the floor. The third umpire though is still having a closer look at it. The big screen shows OUT! WOW! Just incredible. Daryl Mitchell strikes on his third delivery and Sarfaraz Ahmed has to walk back on 78 runs. He will be surely gutted. New Zealand have a sniff here.

New Zealand bowlers have been very disciplined with their lines and lengths and were rewarded with a sole wicket but a huge one, as they got rid of the set batter in Imam-ul-Haq who was scoring runs for fun. It was the skipper, Tim Southee who found the breakthrough. The Kiwis will be very happy with their performance this morning. They will now be hoping to come back out and create some new problems for Pakistan with the second new ball which is due in just 6 overs. Will New Zealand be able to find early wickets when they come on? Or will Pakistan find a match-saving partnership from their current pair? To find out, do join us at 1.10 pm IST (7.40 am GMT) for the post-Lunch session.

Pakistan would be fairly happy with the way they have ended the morning session on the moving day. Imam-ul-Haq and Saud Shakeel came out at the crease and followed the same pattern wherein Imam-ul-Haq was the aggressor and the latter played the second fiddle. Although, they were put under the pump by the consistent bowling of the Kiwis which affected the run flow. Soon, Imam-ul-Haq lost his concentration and slipped out 17 runs short of his ton. Later, Sarfaraz Ahmed came in and stitched a gritty stand of 42 runs with Saud Shakeel to make sure that they do not lose any more wicket before the Lunch break. Pakistan though still trail by 225 runs and need to make sure they do no lose an early wicket in the afternoon session.

Well, this Test match still hangs in the balance. Both the teams have a great opportunity to shift the momentum in the remaining period of the moving day. So coming to the stats of this morning session, New Zealand were able to add one more wicket to their tally as they gave away 70 runs in return in the 27 overs played. There is still a lot to play for in this Test match.

Imam-ul-Haq is up for a chat and he says that the incident with Babar Azam is part of the game and it can not be controlled. Says that they haven't played much Test cricket at home and it is a new challenge for them. Claims that he is working hard and he has been scoring runs in first-class cricket so he is grateful that things are going his way. Mentions that he has practiced a lot and when he dances around the crease he gets multiple options. Ends by saying that to score runs in Pakistan, they need to be really good against spin.

Pitch Report - Bazid Khan says the pitch is still very good for batting. He is joined by Waqar who mentions that New Zealand are playing with two pacers and three spinners. Mentions that the pacers need to maintain the outside off stump line and the spinners could get some extra bounce on this wicket. Reckons that the batters need to be patient and pick their shots on this wicket.

Pakistan will be happy with the way they ended their day but still have a steep mountain to climb as they have a deficit of 295 runs. Will they be able to reduce the lead? Or will the New Zealand bowlers be able to cause any damage early on? We shall find out soon.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 3 of the second Test match between Pakistan and New Zealand. This day is also considered to be the moving day in Test cricket. This game is evenly poised and it all depends on which side gets a good start in the morning session.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Pakistan, on the other hand, would feel that they let go many opportunities to take a more stronger position in this game. They got three wickets early in the day but just could not find a way to break the final wicket stand and as a result, New Zealand who were struggling to get to 350 ended up falling just one run short of 450. With the bat too, all three wickets they lost were because of the mistakes of the batters rather than good deliveries getting them out. Both Abdullah Shafique and Shan Masood got good starts but played an expensive shot and paid the price while the skipper, Babar Azam’s promising innings was cut short by a big misunderstanding between him and Imam-ul-Haq. However, Imam-ul-Haq should be credited with the way he kept his composure after running out his skipper and this 55 runs partnership with Saud has made sure that Pakistan do not explode in the final session. Will we see more application from Pakistani batters on Day 3? We shall find out on Day 3 of this Test match which starts at 10.30 am IST (5 am GMT) on Wednesday, 4th of January. Do join us for the build-up. Cheers!

The heroes of the day for New Zealand were Matt Henry and Ajaz Patel without any doubt. They stitched together a record-breaking stand of 104 for the 10th wicket and took New Zealand to a pole position after they lost three wickets early in the morning session. Henry scored unbeaten 68 with the bat and then came out with the ball with equal zeal and might and got an early wicket of Abdullah Shafique. He also showed his ability to reverse the ball as he bowled with some great rhythm in the final session. Patel too got a wicket to back up his brilliant effort with the bat and though New Zealand would have liked one or two wickets more at the end of Day 2, they would be pretty pleased with their overall effort on the day. They would be looking to get some early wickets on Day 3 but the fact that they got the wicket of Babar Azam wrapped up in a gift hamper as a new year’s gift on this placid deck should encourage them going forward in this Test match.

A gruelling day of Test cricket comes to an end! The final session turned out to be a good classical Test cricket session where both the bowlers and batters were testing out the patience of each other with some disciplined cricket. Pakistan have done well to lose only one wicket in the evening session but have to say, with the lead of 295 under their belt, New Zealand would be the happier side with how things panned out on Day 2.

The third and the final session on Day 2 is set to begin. The New Zealand players take the field. Followed by Babar Azam and Imam-ul-Haq who walk out with their blades. It will be Ajaz Patel to start with the ball.
... Day 2, Session 3 ...

Well! The second session on Day 2 turned out to be a short one as the first session was dragged longer by 30 minutes as Pakistan tried to hunt down the final wicket but were unable to do so. The final pair for Kiwi came out to bat in the post-Lunch session but could only add 16 runs before getting all out for 449 runs. Soon, Pakistan batters came out to bat. Abdullah Shafique seemed to be in a really good form as he raced to 19 runs off 32 balls but perished to a short ball. Shan Masood then came in and provided with a solid counterpunch with his aggressive approach but could not last for long. For Kiwis, Matt Henry and Ajaz Patel have been brilliant for them so far on Day 2, first with the bat and now with the ball in hand. The visitors might think they have their noses in front here and would be itching to come back out on the field to take the game away from Pakistan. The final session on Day 2 will begin at 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT). Do join us to find out how things pan out.
